# Apparatus for Stunning Live Poultry Prior to Slaughter

## Field of the Invention

The present invention concerns an apparatus for stunning live poultry intended for slaughter. The stunning is accomplished by means of a gas mixture containing a stunning gas, whereby the animals remain within their containers throughout the stunning process. This approach allows the poultry to be handled with minimal disturbance, as the animals are not removed from their containers prior to being stunned.

## General Configuration of the Apparatus

The apparatus comprises a stunning chamber that is subdivided into at least two distinct stunning zones. On the inlet side of the chamber, an introduction station is provided for receiving the containers of live poultry, while a discharge station is arranged on the outlet side for removing the containers once the stunning process has been completed.

To facilitate the movement of the containers through the apparatus, at least one transport conveyor is provided. This conveyor advances each container in the transport direction, guiding it through the successive stunning zones from the introduction station to the discharge station in a continuous and controlled manner.

## Distinguishing Feature of the Invention

The key feature that distinguishes the present invention from prior arrangements lies in the configuration of the gas delivery means. Specifically, the gas delivery means includes at least one injection pipe that is movable relative to the container. This mobility enables the injection pipe to be detachably connected to a container and subsequently detached from it as required during the course of the stunning operation.

By virtue of this arrangement, each container can be filled with the gas mixture while it is detachably connected to the injection pipe. This targeted delivery of the stunning gas directly to the individual container ensures an efficient and effective stunning process, while the movable and detachable nature of the injection pipe accommodates the continuous transport of the containers through the stunning zones.

## Scope of the Invention

In addition to the apparatus described above, the invention further encompasses a corresponding arrangement embodying these features, as well as a corresponding method for stunning live poultry intended for slaughter in accordance with the principles set out herein.

# Apparatus and Method for Stunning Live Poultry Prior to Slaughter

## Field of the Invention

This invention concerns an apparatus and method for stunning live poultry in containers before slaughter using a stunning gas mixture. The apparatus employs a stunning chamber with multiple zones, transport conveyors, and gas delivery means to render poultry unconscious in a humane and efficient manner prior to the slaughtering process.

## Background of the Invention

In modern poultry processing, live birds are transported to slaughter facilities in stackable containers or crates. Prior to slaughter, it is both a legal requirement in many jurisdictions and an ethical imperative to render the animals unconscious to minimize distress and suffering. Gas stunning, using controlled mixtures of gases such as carbon dioxide, inert gases, or combinations thereof, has become a widely accepted method for achieving humane stunning while the birds remain within their transport containers, thereby reducing handling stress and injury.

Conventional gas stunning systems typically flood an entire chamber with the stunning gas mixture. While functional, such systems suffer from several drawbacks. Flooding an entire chamber requires large volumes of gas, much of which is not effectively delivered to the birds themselves. Furthermore, uneven distribution of gas throughout the chamber can result in inconsistent stunning, with some birds receiving insufficient exposure while others are over-exposed. These inefficiencies increase operating costs and can compromise both animal welfare and processing throughput.

## Summary of the Invention

The present invention addresses these shortcomings through an improved stunning apparatus. The stunning chamber is divided into multiple zones, allowing birds to progress through successive stages of gas exposure as they are conveyed through the system. Transport conveyors move the containers holding the live poultry through these zones in a continuous or indexed manner, while gas delivery means supply the stunning gas mixture to the birds.

The key innovation of this invention is a movable injection pipe that detachably connects to each individual container. Rather than relying solely on ambient gas flooding of the chamber, the movable injection pipe engages with a given container, forms a connection with it, and delivers the stunning gas directly and precisely into that container. This targeted approach enables the controlled filling of individual containers with the gas mixture, ensuring that each group of birds receives an appropriate and consistent dose.

## Detailed Description

In a typical embodiment, containers of live poultry are loaded onto the transport conveyor at the entrance of the stunning chamber. As the conveyor advances, the containers pass sequentially through the multiple zones of the chamber. Each zone may be configured to deliver a different concentration or composition of the stunning gas mixture, allowing for a graduated stunning process that progressively induces unconsciousness in a manner that reduces aversive reactions in the birds.

Within one or more of these zones, a movable injection pipe is provided. This injection pipe is arranged to move into alignment with an individual container as it arrives at a designated position. The pipe then detachably connects to the container, establishing a sealed or substantially sealed connection to a corresponding inlet or opening on the container. Once connected, the gas delivery means supplies the stunning gas mixture through the injection pipe directly into the interior of the container.

By delivering gas directly into each container, the apparatus ensures that the gas is concentrated where it is needed—around the birds themselves—rather than being dispersed throughout the entire chamber volume. After the container has been filled and the birds have received the required exposure, the injection pipe detaches from the container, and the conveyor advances the container to the next position or zone. The injection pipe may then return to connect with a subsequent container, repeating the cycle.

The movable nature of the injection pipe allows it to accommodate the movement of containers along the conveyor and to service multiple containers in sequence. In certain embodiments, a plurality of injection pipes may be provided to service several containers simultaneously, further increasing throughput.

## Advantages of the Invention

The targeted gas filling made possible by the movable, detachable injection pipe provides several significant advantages over conventional flooding systems:

- **Improved efficiency:** By directing the stunning gas precisely into individual containers, the apparatus reduces gas wastage and lowers overall gas consumption, thereby reducing operating costs.

- **Enhanced effectiveness:** Direct injection ensures consistent and uniform exposure of the birds to the stunning gas, improving the reliability of the stunning process and better safeguarding animal welfare.

- **Consistency:** Each container receives a controlled dose, minimizing the variability inherent in chamber-flooding methods.

- **Flexibility:** The multi-zone configuration, combined with targeted injection, allows the stunning process to be tailored to the specific requirements of the poultry and the applicable welfare standards.

In summary, the present invention provides an apparatus and method for stunning live poultry that combines a multi-zone stunning chamber, transport conveyors, and gas delivery means with a movable injection pipe that detachably connects to each container. This arrangement enables targeted gas filling of individual containers, thereby improving both the efficiency and the effectiveness of the stunning process while promoting the humane treatment of the animals prior to slaughter.

# Patent Abstract

## Apparatus for Gas Stunning of Live Poultry Prior to Slaughter

An apparatus for humanely stunning live poultry using a controlled gas mixture prior to slaughter is disclosed. The apparatus comprises a stunning chamber, a transport conveyor system, and a gas injection system operating in coordinated arrangement to render poultry unconscious in a consistent and welfare-compliant manner.

The stunning chamber defines an enclosed, substantially gas-tight interior configured to maintain a controlled atmosphere. The chamber includes an inlet aperture and an outlet aperture and is dimensioned to accommodate a plurality of poultry containers moving therethrough. In certain embodiments, the chamber comprises multiple vertically or horizontally arranged zones, each maintaining a progressively increasing gas concentration to provide a graduated induction of unconsciousness.

The transport conveyor extends through the stunning chamber and is configured to convey the poultry, retained within crates, modules, or on a moving belt, along a predetermined path through the successive treatment zones at a controlled residence time. The conveyor operates at a variable speed to ensure sufficient exposure of the poultry to the stunning atmosphere for effective and reliable stunning.

The gas injection system is in fluid communication with the stunning chamber and is configured to introduce a stunning gas mixture, such as carbon dioxide, an inert gas, or a combination thereof, into one or more of the chamber zones. The gas injection system includes a gas source, one or more distribution manifolds, and a plurality of injection nozzles positioned to establish and maintain a defined gas concentration gradient within the chamber. One or more sensors monitor gas concentration, temperature, and flow parameters, and a control unit regulates the gas injection system and conveyor speed in response to the monitored parameters to maintain predetermined stunning conditions.

The apparatus provides improved animal welfare, consistent stunning efficacy, and enhanced operational efficiency in poultry processing operations.

A poultry stunning device is disclosed for immobilizing birds prior to processing. The device comprises a plurality of stunning zones configured to receive containers holding poultry, wherein each stunning zone is adapted to sequentially or simultaneously process the birds contained therein. A movable injection pipe is provided that is selectively positionable to establish fluid communication with the containers holding the birds. The injection pipe is configured to deliver a stunning agent, such as a gas or gaseous mixture, into the interior of the containers to induce a stunned state in the poultry. The movable injection pipe traverses between the multiple stunning zones, enabling controlled and efficient distribution of the stunning agent to successive containers as they advance through the device. # Patent-Style Summary: Apparatus and Method for Gas-Stunning of Poultry in Containers

## Field of the Invention

The present invention relates to an apparatus and method for the controlled gas-stunning of poultry, wherein said poultry remains housed within transport or holding containers during the stunning process. More particularly, the invention concerns a system for the introduction of a stunning gas or gas mixture into a plurality of stacked containers by means of detachable injection pipes.

## Background of the Invention

In the processing of poultry, it is desirable to render birds unconscious prior to slaughter in a manner that reduces stress, minimizes physical handling, and improves both animal welfare and carcass quality. Conventional stunning methods frequently require the removal of live birds from their containers, resulting in increased handling, potential injury, and reduced throughput. There exists a need for an apparatus permitting the stunning of poultry directly within their containers, while ensuring uniform gas distribution and operational efficiency.

## Summary of the Invention

According to the present invention, there is provided an apparatus for gas-stunning poultry comprising:

- **(a)** a stunning chamber or enclosure adapted to receive one or more containers holding live poultry;
- **(b)** a supply source for a stunning gas or gas mixture;
- **(c)** a distribution manifold in fluid communication with said supply source; and
- **(d)** a plurality of injection pipes connected to said manifold and arranged to deliver the stunning gas into the interior of said containers.

The apparatus is configured such that the stunning gas is introduced substantially uniformly across the containers, thereby ensuring consistent and humane stunning of the poultry contained therein.

## Characterizing Feature

**Characterized in that** the injection pipes are **detachably mounted** to the distribution manifold, such that each injection pipe may be independently coupled to and decoupled from the manifold without disassembly of the surrounding apparatus.

By virtue of said detachable configuration, the injection pipes may be selectively engaged with the containers during the stunning operation and subsequently withdrawn to permit unobstructed loading, unloading, and conveyance of the containers. This detachable arrangement further facilitates cleaning, maintenance, and replacement of individual injection pipes, and permits the apparatus to be readily adapted to containers of differing dimensions or configurations.

## Advantages

The invention thereby provides:

1. Reduced handling of live poultry, improving animal welfare;
2. Uniform and reliable gas distribution to each container;
3. Enhanced operational flexibility through interchangeable, detachable injection pipes;
4. Simplified cleaning and maintenance; and
5. Improved throughput within poultry processing operations.

---

*Note: This document is provided as a formal drafting aid in patent-style format. For any filing intended to secure enforceable rights, review by a qualified patent attorney or agent is recommended to ensure compliance with jurisdictional requirements and adequacy of claim scope.*

# Patent Abstract

## Apparatus and Method for Anaesthetising Poultry Using Stunning Gas

**Abstract:**

An apparatus for anaesthetising poultry comprising a multi-station conveying system for transporting live poultry through a controlled gas atmosphere for humane stunning prior to processing. The machine includes an **introduction station** configured to receive and load live poultry from transport containers onto a continuous conveying mechanism, wherein said introduction station comprises a loading platform and a metering assembly for regulating the throughput of birds entering the treatment zone at a predetermined rate.

The apparatus further comprises a **treatment tunnel** defining a sealed or semi-sealed chamber containing at least one stunning gas atmosphere, wherein the gas comprises a controlled concentration of carbon dioxide, an inert gas, or a mixture thereof. The conveying system transports the poultry through progressively increasing gas concentration zones to induce anaesthesia in a graduated manner, thereby reducing distress to the birds.

A **discharge station** is positioned at the terminal end of the conveying system for receiving the anaesthetised poultry and transferring said poultry to downstream processing equipment. The discharge station comprises an unloading mechanism and, optionally, a monitoring assembly for verifying the anaesthetic state of the discharged poultry.

The apparatus includes a gas management subsystem having supply conduits, concentration sensors, and a control unit configured to regulate gas composition, flow rate, and residence time within the treatment tunnel.

**Method Claims:**

The invention further encompasses a method for anaesthetising poultry comprising the steps of: (a) loading live poultry at the introduction station onto the conveying system; (b) transporting the poultry through the treatment tunnel while exposing said poultry to a controlled stunning gas atmosphere of increasing concentration over a predetermined residence time; (c) monitoring and regulating the gas concentration to achieve a target anaesthetic state; and (d) discharging the anaesthetised poultry at the discharge station for subsequent processing.

The method may further comprise the step of adjusting conveying speed as a function of measured gas concentration and desired residence time to ensure consistent and humane stunning of the poultry.
